findings.issue_text: `include_website_name` is dead code because Discourse invokes conditional-inclusion hooks with a question mark (`include_website_name?`), so the guard is never called and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting a null key when no website is set

The `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` check does naive string-suffix matching with no public-suffix awareness, causing instances on subdomains of shared domains (e.g., something.github.io) to display unrelated third-party sites as full paths of the forum
Sibling subdomains of different depths are handled inconsistently (website a.example.com on instance b.example.com only handled when segment counts match exactly)
`URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three separate times per serialization (lines 140, 143, 145), creating redundant recomputation and maintenance risk
Query strings are dropped from displayed website names (e.g., `http://example.com/page?x=1` displays as `example.com/page`)
Missing test for the www-vs-forum sibling-domain branch (same label count, different registrable domains) which returns bare website_host — the false leg of the branch is never verified

No test for a website whose host is nil or unparseable URI (e.g. 'example.com/user' with no scheme), leaving unverified the behavior of website_name being absent and the interplay with include_website_name sending website_name: null while website is set

Host comparison in user_serializer.rb:141 is case-sensitive, so http://Example.com/user against instance example.com fails the equality check and drops the complete path — hosts should be compared case-insensitively per RFC 3986

website_name is added to untrusted_attributes but no spec verifies it is consistently absent on the anonymous/limited serializers or which surfaces (e.g. user card templates) receive website_name — card template paths are untested

Trailing-slash/empty-path edge case unaddressed: for http://example.com/ with matching host, website_name becomes 'example.com/' showing a dangling slash where old UI showed clean 'example.com', with no test covering same-domain website with empty or '/' path

Sibling subdomain branch (elsif) in user_serializer.rb:141 shows full URL path for websites on different subdomains (e.g. forum.example.com vs shop.example.com), violating the stated intent of full path only for same domain
Same-domain comparison at user_serializer.rb:137 (website_host == discourse_host) is case- and port-sensitive, failing to show full path for valid mixed-case website URLs like Example.com

URI(website.to_s).host is lowercased by Ruby's URI parser while Discourse.current_hostname is returned verbatim, so mixed-case hostname configuration never matches and the 'show complete path' branch never triggers
Same-domain predicate is asymmetric and misses www↔apex and sibling/nested subdomain cases, causing inconsistent truncated display for equivalent local domains
Repeated URI(website.to_s) parsing and split('.') calls in the serializer hot path, with three hand-maintained parallel comparisons inviting drift
include_website_name returns true while website_name can be nil (e.g. malformed website values), leaving an always-null website_name key in the JSON payload due to inconsistent predicates

The elsif branch in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140-145 returns a full path display for sibling subdomains (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com) that are neither the instance host nor its parent, with no test coverage and a misleading inline comment

The include_website_name guard checks website.present? but website_name returns nil when URI(website).host is nil (e.g. scheme-less input like 'example.com'), causing the website row to be hidden entirely from the profile template

Pre-existing spec fixture was silently changed from 'http://example.com' to 'http://example.com/user', deleting the only coverage of bare-domain (path-less) website input, leaving the website_host + URI(website).path concatenation with empty path untested

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:66–93 — the three new test cases map one-to-one onto the three implementation branches, so no test exercises the subdomain-of-instance-host case (e.g. website 'http://a.example.com/user' with Discourse.current_hostname = 'example.com'), where website_name falls into the else branch and returns only 'a.example.com', dropping '/user' — the exact UX regression the PR claims to fix

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb — the sibling-of-instance check runs in the wrong direction: discourse_host.ends_with?('.a.example.com') is checked instead of website_host.ends_with?('.' << discourse_host), so subdomain URLs of the instance host are mishandled

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — the new include_website_name method has zero test coverage, including the invalid-URI path where website is present but unparseable, so the payload carries website_name: nil with include_website_name true; a future change to include_website_name could silently alter API output since nothing pins this JSON contract
app/assets/javascripts/controllers/user.js.es6:17–21 — the deleted websiteName computed property is replaced by model.website_name with no accompanying frontend test change

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — the serializer tests stub Discourse.current_hostname, so no case covers real hostname values like 'example.com:8080' where URI(...) parsing and ends_with? compare against a host that never includes the port, silently diverging from production hostname resolution
website_name serializer returns nil for scheme-less websites (e.g. example.com/user without http://), causing the profile to show no website line while website is present
Path-append logic drops query strings and fragments when building website_name (URI(...).path only strips scheme/host, dropping query parameters)
URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil silently swallows unparseable websites, causing the profile website row to disappear entirely with no log or user feedback while the API still returns website
Old client-side code (website.split("/")[2]) displayed a host fragment for strings the new server-side URI() rejects (e.g. 'http://bad url' old: displayed; new: nil, row dropped)

URI(website.to_s) is re-parsed up to three times per serialization and the first parse result is thrown away, creating redundant parsing and a subtle maintenance trap where the rescue only guards the first parse

Hand-rolled three-way domain comparison with label-count branches and ends_with? check disagrees for multi-label TLDs (e.g. www.example.co.uk vs example.co.uk), causing inconsistent display of the full path for the same registrable domain

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `include_website_name` is dead code because Discourse invokes conditional-inclusion hooks with a question mark (`include_website_name?`), so the guard is never called and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting a null key when no website is set

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `:website_name` to the serializer attributes and defines an inclusion guard as `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In Discourse serializers, conditional inclusion hooks are typically named `include_<attr>?`; if that convention applies here, this guard won’t be invoked, so `website_name` will be serialized regardless and will evaluate to `nil` when `website` is blank (since `website_name` returns early when `website_host.nil?`). That would expose a null `website_name` key unintentionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` check does naive string-suffix matching with no public-suffix awareness, causing instances on subdomains of shared domains (e.g., something.github.io) to display unrelated third-party sites as full paths of the forum

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the suffix check is `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, which only returns true when the forum hostname is a subdomain of the *exact* `website_host` (e.g., `forums.example.com` ends with `.example.com`). For the cited shared-domain case `something.github.io`, an unrelated third-party site would have `website_host` like `other.github.io`, and `something.github.io` does **not** end with `.other.github.io`, so it would *not* display the full path—only `website_host`. While the logic is naive about public suffixes, the specific behavior claimed in the finding is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling subdomains of different depths are handled inconsistently (website a.example.com on instance b.example.com only handled when segment counts match exactly)

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, sibling subdomains are only treated as “same site” when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` (the `elsif` branch). If the instance is a deeper/shallower sibling (e.g., `forums.b.example.com` vs `a.example.com`), it falls through to the `else` branch, which only checks `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (parent/child), and will return just `website_host` without appending the path. This matches the finding that sibling subdomains of different depths aren’t handled consistently by the current logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three separate times per serialization (lines 140, 143, 145), creating redundant recomputation and maintenance risk

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is invoked multiple times: once to compute `website_host = URI(...).host` and again in each branch when concatenating `+ URI(website.to_s).path`. This is redundant recomputation (and repeats the `rescue nil` protection only for the first parse), creating minor performance overhead and maintainability risk. It’s not a functional defect shown by the diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Query strings are dropped from displayed website names (e.g., `http://example.com/page?x=1` displays as `example.com/page`)

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` serializer method builds the display string using `URI(website.to_s).host` and (in some cases) `URI(website.to_s).path`, but never appends `URI(...).query` (or `request_uri`). The template now displays `{{model.website_name}}`, so a URL like `http://example.com/page?x=1` will display as `example.com/page` while the actual link `href` remains `model.website`. This is a real, diff-grounded edge case in the new display-name logic, not a broken link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for the www-vs-forum sibling-domain branch (same label count, different registrable domains) which returns bare website_host — the false leg of the branch is never verified

adjudication.rationale:
The new `UserSerializer#website_name` adds a nontrivial sibling-subdomain branch:
```rb
elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
  website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
end
```
The added specs cover (1) different domain with 2 labels (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`) which hits the final `else`, (2) exact match, and (3) parent-domain case (`forums.example.com`). No spec exercises the `elsif` branch at all, and therefore its false leg (same label count, different registrable domains => return bare `website_host`) is unverified, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for a website whose host is nil or unparseable URI (e.g. 'example.com/user' with no scheme), leaving unverified the behavior of website_name being absent and the interplay with include_website_name sending website_name: null while website is set

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` using `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early when `website_host.nil?`, while `include_website_name` is `website.present?`. This means a present-but-unparseable/no-scheme website (e.g. `example.com/user`) would likely serialize `website_name: null` even though `website` is set. The updated spec only covers well-formed `http://...` URLs and does not test the nil/unparseable-host branch or the include/serialization behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host comparison in user_serializer.rb:141 is case-sensitive, so http://Example.com/user against instance example.com fails the equality check and drops the complete path — hosts should be compared case-insensitively per RFC 3986

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` is compared to `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` using `==` (and later `ends_with?`) without normalizing case. Since `URI(...).host` can preserve the original case from the URL (e.g., `Example.com`), a same-domain URL with different host casing will fail the `website_host == discourse_host` branch and return only the host (or otherwise miss appending the path), dropping the expected `+ URI(...).path` behavior. This is a correctness issue in the newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: website_name is added to untrusted_attributes but no spec verifies it is consistently absent on the anonymous/limited serializers or which surfaces (e.g. user card templates) receive website_name — card template paths are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `website_name` added to `UserSerializer` and corresponding usage in `user/user.hbs`, plus new serializer specs that explicitly assert `json[:website_name]` behavior under different hostnames. The finding claims lack of specs for “anonymous/limited serializers” and “user card template paths”, but no anonymous/limited serializers or card templates appear in this diff, so that concern can’t be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Trailing-slash/empty-path edge case unaddressed: for http://example.com/ with matching host, website_name becomes 'example.com/' showing a dangling slash where old UI showed clean 'example.com', with no test covering same-domain website with empty or '/' path

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, when `website_host == discourse_host` (and also in the “parent domain” branch), it returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. For `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `/`, so `website_name` becomes `example.com/`. The previous client-side `websiteName` logic (`website.split("/")[2]`) would have displayed `example.com` without the trailing slash, so this diff introduces a UI regression for same-host (or parent-host) websites with an empty or `/` path. The added specs only cover `/user`, not `/` or empty path, so the edge case is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling subdomain branch (elsif) in user_serializer.rb:141 shows full URL path for websites on different subdomains (e.g. forum.example.com vs shop.example.com), violating the stated intent of full path only for same domain

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, the `elsif` branch is explicitly designed to include the path for sibling subdomains when they share the same parent domain (comment: `# www.example.com == forum.example.com`) via `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host`. So showing `.../path` for `forum.example.com` vs `shop.example.com` is intentional per the diff, not a violation of the implemented/stated logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same-domain comparison at user_serializer.rb:137 (website_host == discourse_host) is case- and port-sensitive, failing to show full path for valid mixed-case website URLs like Example.com

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` compares `website_host == discourse_host` and later uses `ends_with?` with `website_host` (both case-sensitive). Since `website_host` comes from `URI(website.to_s).host` without any downcasing/normalization in the diff, a user-entered URL like `http://Example.com/user` would yield `website_host = "Example.com"`, and if `Discourse.current_hostname` is `"example.com"` the equality/ends_with? checks fail and the method falls back to returning only the host (dropping the path), contrary to intended same-domain behavior. The finding’s mention of port-sensitivity isn’t supported by the diff (ports aren’t compared), but the case-sensitivity issue is real and affects behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(website.to_s).host is lowercased by Ruby's URI parser while Discourse.current_hostname is returned verbatim, so mixed-case hostname configuration never matches and the 'show complete path' branch never triggers

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the domain-matching logic (`website_host == discourse_host`, and subsequent comparisons) is case-sensitive and does not normalize either value. If `website_host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` differ only by case, the "same host"/"parent domain" branches won’t trigger and `website_name` may incorrectly omit the path. The diff shows no downcasing/normalization safeguards around these comparisons.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same-domain predicate is asymmetric and misses www↔apex and sibling/nested subdomain cases, causing inconsistent truncated display for equivalent local domains

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` treats “same/local domain” cases inconsistently. It includes the path when `website_host == discourse_host`, when the website host is a parent of the instance host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), and for some sibling subdomains with equal label counts. But it does not handle the inverse www↔apex case (e.g. `website_host = www.example.com`, `discourse_host = example.com`), which will fall through to returning only `website_host` (dropping the path). This asymmetry is visible from the conditional structure and can lead to inconsistent truncated display for domains that are effectively equivalent within the same site family, but the diff doesn’t establish a hard correctness requirement that www/apex must be treated as “same,” so it’s best framed as an edge-case/design gap rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated URI(website.to_s) parsing and split('.') calls in the serializer hot path, with three hand-maintained parallel comparisons inviting drift

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the diff shows repeated parsing and string splitting: `URI(website.to_s)` is called multiple times (for `.host` and again for `.path` in multiple branches), and `discourse_host.split('.')` / `website_host.split('.')` are recomputed several times within the same method. This is a real maintainability/performance concern in serializer code (potentially called frequently), but it does not constitute a verifiable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name returns true while website_name can be nil (e.g. malformed website values), leaving an always-null website_name key in the JSON payload due to inconsistent predicates

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` can return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` fails or is missing (`rescue nil` then `return if website_host.nil?`). However, `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so a non-empty but malformed/unparseable `website` will still satisfy the include predicate while producing a `nil` value. That mismatch can lead to `website_name: null` being serialized instead of omitting the field, which aligns with the finding’s claim of inconsistent predicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The elsif branch in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140-145 returns a full path display for sibling subdomains (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com) that are neither the instance host nor its parent, with no test coverage and a misleading inline comment

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, the new `website_name` method has a nontrivial `elsif` branch for same-label-count subdomains (`website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && > 2`) that conditionally returns `website_host + URI(...).path` when the parent domains match (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added spec covers (1) different domain => host only, (2) same domain => host+path, and (3) website domain is parent of instance domain => host+path, but does not cover this sibling-subdomain branch at all. The inline comment `# www.example.com == forum.example.com` is also potentially misleading because the branch only returns the full path when the parent domains match; otherwise it returns just `website_host`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The include_website_name guard checks website.present? but website_name returns nil when URI(website).host is nil (e.g. scheme-less input like 'example.com'), causing the website row to be hidden entirely from the profile template

adjudication.rationale: In the serializer, `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, but `website_name` can still return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil (it rescues to nil). The template now renders the website display only under `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so a non-empty but non-parseable (hostless) `website` would not be shown. The diff shows this guard/value mismatch; whether scheme-less websites can occur depends on validations not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing spec fixture was silently changed from 'http://example.com' to 'http://example.com/user', deleting the only coverage of bare-domain (path-less) website input, leaving the website_host + URI(website).path concatenation with empty path untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the serializer spec fixture from `http://example.com` to `http://example.com/user` (see `user_serializer_spec.rb`), and all new `website_name` expectations also use a URL with a path. This removes explicit test coverage for the bare-domain/path-less input. In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, multiple branches return `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`; when the path is empty, that concatenation behavior is untested by the updated spec. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in edge-case coverage rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:66–93 — the three new test cases map one-to-one onto the three implementation branches, so no test exercises the subdomain-of-instance-host case (e.g. website 'http://a.example.com/user' with Discourse.current_hostname = 'example.com'), where website_name falls into the else branch and returns only 'a.example.com', dropping '/user' — the exact UX regression the PR claims to fix

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `else` branch (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(...).path : website_host`) will return only the host (no path) when the website is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. website_host `a.example.com`, discourse_host `example.com`). The added specs only cover: (1) different domains -> host only, (2) same domain -> host+path, (3) website is parent of instance -> host+path. No new test covers the subdomain-of-instance-host scenario, so that edge case is unexercised by the suite even though it’s a distinct behavior in the new branching logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb — the sibling-of-instance check runs in the wrong direction: discourse_host.ends_with?('.a.example.com') is checked instead of website_host.ends_with?('.' << discourse_host), so subdomain URLs of the instance host are mishandled

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the final branch explicitly checks whether the *instance host* is a subdomain of the *website host* via `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, matching the comment `# example.com == forum.example.com` (i.e., instance = forum.example.com, website = example.com). The finding claims this check is “in the wrong direction” and should instead test `website_host.ends_with?("." << discourse_host)`, but that would represent the opposite relationship (website being a subdomain of the instance), which is not what this branch is labeled/implementing. Based on the diff, the finding misreads the intended logic and the actual condition used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — the new include_website_name method has zero test coverage, including the invalid-URI path where website is present but unparseable, so the payload carries website_name: nil with include_website_name true; a future change to include_website_name could silently alter API output since nothing pins this JSON contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` plus `include_website_name` in `user_serializer.rb`, where `website_name` rescues URI parsing errors to `nil` (`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`) but `include_website_name` includes the field whenever `website.present?`. The added spec only tests valid URLs and does not cover `include_website_name` behavior or the unparseable-URI case where `website` is present yet `website_name` becomes `nil` while still being included in the JSON payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/controllers/user.js.es6:17–21 — the deleted websiteName computed property is replaced by model.website_name with no accompanying frontend test change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the `websiteName` computed property in `controllers/user.js.es6` and switches the template to `model.website_name`, but there’s no evidence in the diff that a missing *frontend* test change is required or that any frontend tests even exist/should be updated. The nontrivial logic was moved to `UserSerializer#website_name` and is covered by added/updated Ruby serializer specs, so the finding reads as an ungrounded expectation rather than a concrete, diff-demonstrable issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — the serializer tests stub Discourse.current_hostname, so no case covers real hostname values like 'example.com:8080' where URI(...) parsing and ends_with? compare against a host that never includes the port, silently diverging from production hostname resolution

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial hostname-comparison logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that assumes `discourse_host` is a plain host (e.g., uses `split('.')` and `ends_with?("." << website_host)`). The new specs only cover stubbed values like `'discourse.org'`, `'example.com'`, and `'forums.example.com'` and do not exercise cases where `Discourse.current_hostname` might include a port (e.g., `'example.com:8080'`), which would change `split('.')` results and make `ends_with?` comparisons fail. The claim about production returning a port isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the missing edge-case coverage for the new comparison logic is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: website_name serializer returns nil for scheme-less websites (e.g. example.com/user without http://), causing the profile to show no website line while website is present

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` is derived via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early if `website_host.nil?`. For scheme-less values like `example.com/user`, Ruby's `URI(...)` treats it as a path and `host` is `nil`, so `website_name` becomes `nil` even though `website` is present. The template was changed to render the website line only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present `website` with a nil `website_name` results in no website line being shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Path-append logic drops query strings and fragments when building website_name (URI(...).path only strips scheme/host, dropping query parameters)

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, when the code decides to append the URL path it uses `URI(website.to_s).path` (and separately `URI(...).host`). In Ruby, `URI(...).path` excludes the query string and fragment, so a website like `http://example.com/user?x=1#bio` would produce `example.com/user` (dropping `?x=1#bio`) in `website_name`. This is a real edge-case/behavior gap in the newly added logic, but the diff doesn’t establish that query/fragment must be preserved in the display name, so it’s not a clearly verifiable defect from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil silently swallows unparseable websites, causing the profile website row to disappear entirely with no log or user feedback while the API still returns website

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` does `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and then `return if website_host.nil?`. Meanwhile `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, so the API can still return `website` but `website_name` will be nil for unparseable URLs. The template was changed to render the website row only when `model.website_name` is present (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so an invalid/unparseable website will cause the website row to disappear with no logging or feedback, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Old client-side code (website.split("/")[2]) displayed a host fragment for strings the new server-side URI() rejects (e.g. 'http://bad url' old: displayed; new: nil, row dropped)

adjudication.rationale: Diff moves `websiteName` from client-side `website.split("/")[2]` to server-side `website_name` via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` (user_serializer.rb). For malformed URLs that still contain slashes (e.g., with spaces), the old split-based extraction could produce a non-empty fragment, while the new code can return `nil`, causing `{{#if model.website_name}}` in user.hbs to hide the entire website display even though `website` is present. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior change for invalid/legacy data, but it’s not clearly a defect without a stated requirement to display malformed URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(website.to_s) is re-parsed up to three times per serialization and the first parse result is thrown away, creating redundant parsing and a subtle maintenance trap where the rescue only guards the first parse

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is called repeatedly (to get `.host` and later `.path`), rather than parsing once and reusing the result. The first call is wrapped with `rescue nil` (`website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`), while later calls (`URI(website.to_s).path`) are not explicitly rescued. With the current code flow, a parse failure in the first call returns early, so it’s not a demonstrated runtime bug, but it is a concrete diff-grounded maintainability/perf issue and the rescue asymmetry could become a trap if the method changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hand-rolled three-way domain comparison with label-count branches and ends_with? check disagrees for multi-label TLDs (e.g. www.example.co.uk vs example.co.uk), causing inconsistent display of the full path for the same registrable domain

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new server-side logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that tries to decide when to append the URL path based on hostname comparisons using `split('.')` label counts and an `ends_with?("." << website_host)` suffix test. This is hand-rolled domain logic without a public-suffix/registrable-domain concept, so it can misclassify “same site” cases depending on how many labels are in the host (e.g., different subdomain depths), which plausibly includes multi-label TLD situations. The diff doesn’t define the intended behavior for these edge cases, so it’s not a provable defect from the PR alone, but it is a concrete correctness risk created by the added logic.
